title: Referrals and repeat work from existing clients for residential cleaning
audience: Solo residential cleaners and owners of small house-cleaning teams who want repeat bookings and referrals from households they have already served.
learningOutcomes: Plan a review or referral request that is made after the client confirms the result and that the client can decline easily.
Write a next-service offer with a date, a scope and a price approach, and schedule the check-in that follows it.
Write referral reward terms, including the condition for payment, before any referral is made.

instruction.heading: Ask once the household has confirmed the clean
instruction.body: Ask for a review or a referral after the household has said the clean matches the checklist, usually at sign-off or when the invoice is paid. Use one sentence, name the next step (a review or the name of one person who might need a clean) and make it easy to say no. Timing matters: one Baylor Keller Center experiment found that a late reminder drew more reviews than an immediate one. That is a single experiment. The American Marketing Association's guidance says the right timing depends on the product, and that experience goods need more time to evaluate. A home clean may be that kind of product, so test the timing on your own clients.

instruction.heading: Ask every household, and use the review link
instruction.body: Google provides a review link or QR code that you can share. Ask every household, not only the ones you expect to praise: filtering who is asked is called review gating, and the vendor Podium says Google treats it as a violation (vendor source; not checked against Google's policy). Never write reviews for clients or invent them. Google bans discounts or goods in exchange for reviews. The ACCC says incentives must be disclosed and must not depend on what the review says (15 July 2026).

instruction.heading: Offer the next clean before the household leaves
instruction.body: At sign-off, propose the next clean with a date and an interval, such as a fortnightly or monthly visit, or a deep clean before a set period. The intervals in this lesson are illustrative choices, not sourced benchmarks. Write the scope, the interval and the price approach, and get the household's confirmation before you change the schedule. A short follow-up after each completed job about a maintenance plan is one approach that a vendor recommends (Housecall Pro, 8 June 2026). If that follow-up is an email or text that promotes a service, check the ACMA rules first.

instruction.heading: Check in and re-contact at times you can deliver
instruction.body: Schedule a short check-in after an interval you test on your own clients. The research did not find a residential benchmark for that interval. Plan re-contact before a busy period only if you can deliver the slots you offer. Keep the message factual and optional. Honour every opt-out within five working days, and record it the day you receive it (ACMA, read 4 November 2026).

instruction.heading: Set referral rewards in writing before anyone refers
instruction.body: Decide the reward, such as a credit on the next clean or a small thank-you, and write down the payment condition, usually that the referred household has booked and completed a paid clean. Stating the referrer's reward in the invitation increased referrals across the studies that Xu, Yu and Tu report (2023). Get the referred household's consent before any referral message is sent, because a referrer's word alone may not be enough (Clayton Utz, 2017, an older source). The tax and contract effect of a credit was not confirmed, so take advice before you start a scheme.

procedure: After each clean is signed off, make one review or referral request, and record what was asked and the answer.
Write the next-clean offer with a date, scope, interval and price approach, and get the household's confirmation.
Schedule the check-in at an interval you have tested, and send it using the electronic message rules.
Plan re-contact before each busy period you can deliver, and leave out anyone who has opted out.
Write the referral reward and its payment condition before the first referral is made.
When a referral books and is paid, apply the reward and record the outcome.
Review each season which requests, offers and timings produced repeat work.

workedExamples.situation: A house cleaner has cleaned a family's home fortnightly for a year (illustrative). After a deep clean, the client says she will recommend the cleaner to her sister, who lives on the same street, and asks what she gets in return.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the cleaner write down before the sister books, and what should the cleaner avoid?
workedExamples.reasoning: The cleaner writes the reward terms first: a credit on the client's next regular clean, the condition that the sister completes a paid clean, and when the credit applies. The client passes on the sister's details, and the cleaner contacts the sister only after she agrees. The cleaner does not promise an amount that is not in writing, does not offer the credit in return for a review, and does not tie any reward to what a review says. If the cleaner is unsure of the tax or contract effect of the credit, he or she checks with an adviser before the scheme starts. The cleaner also accepts only the work that the cleaner's own licence and insurance cover.

equipmentAndPpe: Client record with the sign-off date and the review or referral request made
Next-service offer template with scope, interval and price approach
Calendar of seasonal re-contact dates for the service
No PPE is needed for client follow-up; any site visit follows the site's own safety rules

commonErrors.error: Asking for a review before the household has said the clean is right.
commonErrors.prevention: Ask at sign-off or after payment, once the household has confirmed the result.

commonErrors.error: Offering a referral credit that was never written down.
commonErrors.prevention: Write the reward and its payment condition before any referral, and give the client a copy.

commonErrors.error: Filtering which households are asked for a review.
commonErrors.prevention: Ask every household and let the review link do the rest (review gating is a violation, per Podium's account of Google's policy).

commonErrors.error: Using a household's name, photo or home details in marketing without consent.
commonErrors.prevention: Get consent for each thing you plan to publish, and keep the record.

commonErrors.error: Contacting a household that asked not to hear from you.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep an opt-out list and act on each request within five working days.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Publishing a client's name, photo, review or home detail needs the client's consent for that use. Do not write reviews on a client's behalf. If the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) applies to your business, client details are personal information. The OAIC direct-marketing guidance (modified 5 September 2024) sets out APP 7. Whether the Act applies to your business was not confirmed.

Check-in and re-contact messages sent by email or text can be commercial electronic messages under the Spam Act 2003 (Cth). A message that promotes any service can be commercial even when it is framed as a reminder (Clayton Utz, 2023). The Act's text was not read for this lesson.

Review platforms and referral schemes can have their own rules on incentives. Google bans discounts or goods in exchange for reviews, and the ACCC says incentives must be disclosed. Check each platform's rules before you offer any reward.

A referral does not extend the licence or insurance of the cleaner. Accept only the work that your licence and insurance cover, in the state or territory where the work is done. Licence rules for house cleaning were not researched, so check the rules for each state or territory where you work.

qualityStandard: Every review or referral request is made after sign-off or payment, and it includes an easy way to decline.
Every next-service offer is written, has a date and is confirmed by the client before the schedule changes.
Every referral reward has written terms and a payment condition, and is paid only when that condition is met.
documentationEvidence: Review or referral request log with the date sent and the answer.
Next-service offers with the date, scope, interval and client confirmation.
Referral reward terms with the referral record and payment outcome.
summary: Ask for reviews after the household has confirmed the clean, and make it easy to say no.
Offer the next clean in writing, with a date, before the household leaves.
Set referral rewards and their payment conditions in writing before anyone refers. Gap: no Australian source on residential repeat or referral rates was found.

knowledgeChecks.question: When is the best time to ask a household for a review or referral?
options: Before the clean starts, so the household feels committed
After the household has confirmed the clean matches the checklist
Only after the household has made a complaint

knowledgeChecks.question: A household wants to post a review with its name and a photo of the home. What do you need?
options: The household's consent for that name and photo
Nothing, because the review is positive
Your own view that the photo looks good

knowledgeChecks.question: What should a referral credit look like?
options: Paid to anyone who mentions your name
Decided after the referred household books, based on how keen the referrer seems
Written in advance, with the payment condition stated

knowledgeChecks.question: When should the next clean be proposed to the household?
options: At the end of the clean, with a date

sourceReferences: Baylor Keller Center, 'Wait Just a Minute', https://kellercenter.hankamer.baylor.edu/news/story/2024/wait-just-minute-when-ask-online-reviews, 1 June 2024 (metadata says 13 May 2024). One experiment only. Supports: an immediate reminder reduced reviews and a later reminder raised them.

American Marketing Association, 'Asking for customer reviews at the right time', https://www.ama.org/2023/01/10/asking-for-customer-reviews-at-the-right-time-sooner-is-not-always-better/, 10 January 2023. Supports: the right timing depends on the product; experience goods need more time to evaluate.

Google Help, Business Profile review help page, https://support.google.com/business/answer/3474122?hl=en-GB, no date shown. Supports: a review link or QR code may be shared; discounts or goods in exchange for reviews are banned.

Podium, 'Review gating', https://www.podium.com/article/review-gating, 2 May 2022. Vendor source; its account of Google's position was not checked against Google's policy. Supports: filtering who is asked for a review is called review gating.

ACCC, 'Online reviews for product and services', https://www.accc.gov.au/business/advertising-and-promotions/online-reviews-for-product-and-services, published and updated 15 July 2026. Supports: incentives for reviews must be disclosed and must not depend on what the review says.

ACMA, 'Avoid sending spam', https://www.acma.gov.au/avoid-sending-spam, no date shown; read 2026-11-04 per the research file. Supports: consent, accurate sender details, and an unsubscribe honoured within five working days.

Housecall Pro, 'Recurring service agreements', https://www.housecallpro.com/resources/recurring-service-agreements/, published 8 June 2026, updated 9 June 2026. Vendor source; no statistics used. Supports: a short follow-up after each completed job about a maintenance plan; define in the contract how unused visits roll over.

Xu, Yu and Tu, Journal of Marketing Research 60(2), 2023, https://research.polyu.edu.hk/en/publications/i-will-get-a-reward-too-when-disclosing-the-referrer-reward-incre/. Supports: stating the referrer's reward in the invitation increased referring across the studies reported. No figures used.

Clayton Utz, 'Referrer beware', https://www.claytonutz.com/insights/2017/may/referrer-beware-proceed-with-caution-when-contemplating-refer-a-friend-promotions, 11 May 2017 (older than 2022). Supports: a referrer's word alone may not be enough; get the referred person's consent.

Clayton Utz, 'The ACMA cranks up enforcement', https://www.claytonutz.com/insights/2023/november/the-acma-cranks-up-enforcement-do-your-factual-customer-emails-pass-the-spam-act-test, 9 November 2023. Supports: a service reminder that promotes any service can be a commercial message.

OAIC, 'Direct marketing', https://www.oaic.gov.au/privacy/privacy-guidance-for-organisations-and-government-agencies/organisations/direct-marketing, published 1 May 2019, modified 5 September 2024. Supports: APP 7 governs direct marketing using personal information; opt-out must be simple.

Notes: the intervals used as examples are illustrative choices. The Baylor result is from one experiment. Podium is a vendor source. The Xu et al. study is not a cleaning study and no figures are used from it.

officialReferences.title: Avoid sending spam
officialReferences.covers: Says commercial messages cannot be sent without the recipient's permission or consent; messages must accurately identify the sender and include correct contact details; every commercial message must contain an unsubscribe option under the Spam Act 2003, which the page says sets out responsibilities under Australian law. Does not mention one-to-one messages. Publisher: ACMA.
